cable-diagnostics.description:
Display the results of a time domain reflectometry (TDR) diagnostic test run on an interface.
A TDR test characterizes and locates faults on twisted-pair Ethernet cables. For example, it can detect a broken twisted pair and provide the approximate distance to the break.
Select the port and click the Test button.

NORMAL.label: Normal
NORMAL.description: No cable fault detected for the twisted pair.

OPEN.label: Open
OPEN.description: Lack of continuity between the pins of the twisted-pair.

SHORT.label: Short
SHORT.description: A short-circuit was detected on the twisted pair.

IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH.label: Impedance mismatch
IMPEDANCE_MISMATCH.description: Impedance on the twisted pair is not correct. Possible reasons for an impedance mismatch include: The twisted pair is not connected properly; the twisted pair is damaged; the connector is faulty.

downlink-mu-mimo.label: DL MU-MIMO

uplink-mu-mimo.label: UL MU-MIMO

twt.label: Target Wake Time
twt.tooltip: Target Wake Time (TWT) is a standby time scheduling introduced for the 802.11ax standard. Its primary goal is to conserve mobile clients' battery power and make the network more efficient by reducing bandwidth use and access contention.

finish-notice-alert.router:
Your Keenetic device is switched to the Router Operating Mode.


It is now available at my.keenetic.net.
finish-notice-alert.client:
Your Keenetic device is switched to the Wi-Fi Adapter Operating Mode.


To access your Keenetic device now, connect it to the primary segment of your network:

  1. Place the adapter device within the coverage of your Wi-Fi network.
  2. Press the Wi-Fi Button on the main Keenetic router and the adapter device.
  3. The Internet LED on the adapter device will light up when the connection is successful.

To access the device when disconnected from your network, use the self-assigned IP address 192.168.1.3. Please set your computer IP address somewhere between 192.168.1.4 and 192.168.1.254 before accessing the device in a standalone scenario.


Use any network ports on the adapter device to connect your clients.
finish-notice-alert.repeater:
Your Keenetic device is switched to the Repeater/Extender Operating Mode.


To access your Keenetic device now, connect it to the primary segment of your network:

  1. Place the repeater/extender device within the coverage of your Wi-Fi network and toward the area where you want a stronger Wi-Fi signal.
  2. Press the Wi-Fi Button on the main Keenetic router and the repeater/extender device.
  3. The Internet LED on the repeater/extender device will light up when the connection is successful. Wi-Fi settings will be copied from the main Keenetic router, giving you continuous coverage without changing your wireless clients' settings.

To access the device when disconnected from your network, use the self-assigned IP address 192.168.1.3. Please set your computer IP address somewhere between 192.168.1.4 and 192.168.1.254 before accessing the device in a standalone scenario.


Use any network ports on the repeater/extender device to connect your clients.
finish-notice-alert.extender:
Your Keenetic device is switched to the Extender Operating Mode.


To access your Keenetic device now, connect it to the primary segment of your network:
Option I. Wired connection.

  1. Connect any network port of this Keenetic device to your main router's appropriate primary segment's network port with an Ethernet cable.
  2. The Internet LED on the extender device will light up when the connection is successful.

Option II. Wireless connection.
  1. Place the extender device within the coverage of your Wi-Fi network and toward the area where you want a stronger Wi-Fi signal.
  2. Press the Wi-Fi Button on the main Keenetic router and the extender device.
  3. The Internet LED on the extender device will light up when the connection is successful. Wi-Fi settings will be copied from the main Keenetic router, giving you continuous coverage without changing your wireless clients' settings.

To access the device when disconnected from your network, use the self-assigned IP address 192.168.1.3. Please set your computer IP address somewhere between 192.168.1.4 and 192.168.1.254 before accessing the device in a standalone scenario.


Use any network ports on the extender device to connect your clients.
finish-notice-alert.ap:
Your Keenetic device is switched to the Access point/Extender Operating Mode.


To access your Keenetic device now, connect it to the primary segment of your network:

  1. Connect any network port of this Keenetic device to your main router's appropriate primary segment's network port with an Ethernet cable.
  2. The Internet LED on the access point/extender device will light up when the connection is successful.

To access the device when disconnected from your network, use the self-assigned IP address 192.168.1.3. Please set your computer IP address somewhere between 192.168.1.4 and 192.168.1.254 before accessing the device in a standalone scenario.


Use any network ports on the access point/extender device to connect your clients.
Wireless clients are connected to the access point/extender device using the Wi-Fi network settings specified on the label. You can also change these settings using the device's web interface.

controller.title: Controller
controller.description-with-wizard:
This Keenetic device is in Router Mode and acts as the Controller of your Mesh Wi-Fi System.

To add a new Keenetic device to your Wi-Fi System, switch the new device to Extender Mode, and then connect it to the Controller by simultaneously pressing the Wi-Fi Button on both devices or using the supplied Ethernet cable. When the new Keenetic device appears in the list below, click the Acquire button next to it. The Extender can then be moved to the necessary location to expand your Wi-Fi coverage area.

To switch your Keenetic device to the Extender Mode set the operating mode switch on the side or back panel to position C or B (if position C is not available) or use the web interface to select Extender Mode.
controller.description-no-wizard:
This Keenetic device acts as the Controller of the Mesh Wi-Fi System.

To build the Wi-Fi System, switch a new Keenetic device (Keenetic Buddy devices excepted) to Extender Mode. If the device features a hardware operating mode switch, set it to position C or B; otherwise, use the web interface to select Extender Mode. Connect the new Extender to the Controller network either with the supplied Ethernet cable or by pressing the Wi-Fi Button on both devices. Wait for the Extender tile to appear, click the Acquire button and let the process finish. Then you can move the acquired Extender to the necessary location.

Acquiring the Extender requires it has no admin account password. If you do not see the Extender tile after connecting a new device to your network, or the process fails to finish, reset the new device to the factory default and repeat the procedure.
